Ось що знайшов пошук про новини в Україні у жовтні 2026 року. Найсвіжіші дані датовані 16–18 жовтня.

**Фронт і безпека**
- Суспільне повідомляє про затримання в Харківській області підозрюваного у вбивстві п'яти військових. Новинний архів сайту Суспільне Новини за 16 жовтня 2026 містить низку таких сюжетів.
- За даними Укрінформу, 18 жовтня на Волині ліквідували пожежу на підприємстві після російської атаки.
- Російська дронова атака на Луцьк 14 жовтня призвела до загиблих і поранених, а в Краматорську дрон атакував евакуаційний автомобіль.

**Енергетика та побут**
- В Україні помітно посилили графіки відключення світла: де діє екстрений режим і виникли аварії.
- Укрінформ фіксує екстрені відключення світла, зокрема в Бучанському районі на Київщині.

**Міжнародна підтримка**
- Швеція виділяє Україні новий пакет підтримки на майже 45 мільйонів євро, про це повідомило Суспільне 16 жовтня.
- ЄС затвердив графіки поставок озброєння в рамках кредиту на підтримку України на 2026 рік.
- Європарламент ухвалив резолюцію, в якій підтримав Україну та назвав Держдуму Росії нелегітимною.

**Економіка та політика**
- Кабмін створив комісію для продажу банків «Сенс Банк» і «Укргазбанк» (Укрінформ, 18 жовтня).
- 69% українців підтримують обрання генпрокурора на відкритому конкурсі за участі іноземних експертів, за даними КМІС.
- Радіо Свобода пише, що Трамп домовився з Путіним про експорт дизельного пального, а Україна назвала це «подарунком» Росії. Цей сюжет стосується 10 жовтня.

**Спорт і культура**
- Український футболіст Тутєров дебютував в основі «Сандерленда» у Лізі Європи.
- Українські тенісистки грають у кваліфікації турніру WTA 500 у Нінбо.

**Очікування на жовтень**
Огляд за вересень прогнозував, що жовтень має принести українцям рішення щодо бюджету й воєнного стану та, можливо, нові перемовини про мир.

Зауважу, що деякі джерела мають неоднозначні дати (наприклад, стрічка Радіо Свобода містить сюжети з різних днів), тому для точних подробиць краще перейти за посиланнями на першоджерела, наприклад suspilne.media або ukrinform.ua.

Here's what the search turned up for early-to-mid October 2026. The newest reports are from about October 13–15, so I found nothing from the last few days.

**Civilian casualties from Russian strikes**
- The UN aid office reported that recent Russian attacks on Kharkiv and Kyiv killed residents and injured dozens more. In Kyiv alone, one civilian was reported killed and 11 injured.
- A larger assault on October 7 reportedly killed at least 20 people. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 130 drones, 48 cruise missiles, and an unspecified number of ballistic missiles in the overnight attack. In Pryluki, in the northern Chernihiv region, a Russian missile hit a five-storey residential building, and at least 14 people, including four children, were killed.

**Energy ceasefire and refinery strikes**
- President Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" on a Sunday in early October. Zelensky says Ukraine has not hit Russian refineries since then. He said Kyiv had not received the usual warning from allies of ballistic missile launches before a "particularly vile" attack on Kyiv overnight.
- Reuters and other outlets report that US officials have threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and weapons sales to Ukraine unless it stops attacking Russian refineries. Trump has said the US is still sharing intelligence.
- A later NPR report says Ukraine resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries after the brief pause. Russia, for its part, hit Ukrainian gas facilities after the announced truce.

**Diplomacy**
- Zelenskyy said the U.S. has proposed fresh trilateral peace talks by the end of October, and Ukraine is responding positively to the initiative.
- Russia has pledged to intensify strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities after a drone attack damaged the capital's Northern Bridge over the weekend. Moscow framed these strikes as retaliation for Ukraine's refinery attacks.
- Escalating violence and human rights violations in the war are on the agenda at the UN Security Council following a string of Russian attacks on civilian targets and infrastructure.

Note that my search also returned pages from October 2023 and 2025, which I've left out because they're not about 2026.

Here's what the coverage from October 18, 2026 shows. I didn't find anything specific to October 17.

**US-Ukraine friction**
- Zelensky said on NBC's "Meet the Press" that US intelligence used to detect incoming Russian missile strikes had been restored after a brief pause. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed Sunday that the United States temporarily interrupted intelligence-sharing with Ukraine, and the signal-detection feed is back online.
- Zelensky accused Trump of pressing Kyiv to give in to Moscow, which escalated a week-long row with the US president. Trump responded on Truth Social, saying he didn't want to derail Russia's negotiating track and that he saw "great progress." He also excoriated Zelensky, saying that he "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did."
- The dispute followed a US decision to waive sanctions on Russia's energy sector. Trump, on Friday night, waived sanctions targeting Russia's energy economy.
- Zelensky also offered to stop striking Russian refineries, a request Trump had made to ease high diesel prices, in exchange for more Patriot air-defense missiles. He proposed this in exchange for deliveries of more Patriot air-defense missiles.

**Diplomacy**
- Zelensky said the war "must be brought to an end" and that Kyiv is preparing for the next diplomatic steps. He reported a call with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.

**Strikes and attacks**
- Ukraine carried out a large drone attack on Russia's St. Petersburg region. One target was the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal, according to Russian authorities. Russia's defense ministry said it shot down 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday over various parts of the country.
- Russia struck Ukraine's energy grid overnight. Zelensky said strikes hit substations in several regions, leaving tens of thousands of families without power. Two people were killed and 12 injured after residential buildings were struck overnight, according to his post on X.

Sources differ on framing: Bloomberg and Al Jazeera emphasize the diplomatic fallout, while CNN's headline frames the Ukrainian strike as defiance of Trump's demand to stop hitting Russian energy infrastructure.

content.text:
Here are the three biggest Ukraine stories from 12–19 October 2026:

1. **Ukraine and the US are openly at odds.** On 18 October, Zelensky said Trump was pressing Ukraine to give in to Russia. He also confirmed the US had briefly paused the intelligence it shares on incoming Russian missiles, a dispute that came after Trump lifted sanctions on Russia's energy sector and that Trump answered by saying Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war." ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-10-18/zelenskyy-says-trump-is-pushing-ukraine-to-capitulate-to-russia))

2. **Ukraine went back to hitting Russian energy sites, in defiance of Washington.** A short US-backed "energy ceasefire" collapsed, and Ukraine launched a huge drone attack on the St. Petersburg region, setting an oil terminal on fire; Russia said it shot down 1,015 drones overnight. ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/18/europe/ukraine-russia-drone-attack-trump-intl))

3. **Russian strikes keep killing civilians and cutting power.** Overnight into 18 October, Russia hit substations in several regions, leaving tens of thousands of families without electricity and killing two people. This came after a 13 October attack on Kyiv that Zelensky said allies gave no warning of. ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/18/russias-war-on-ukraine-must-be-brought-to-an-end-zelenskyy-says))

These summaries come from search-result descriptions; I didn't open the full articles. Choosing the "top three" is my own call, and the US-pushed peace talks planned for the end of October were a close fourth.
